Build an online stream-mining stack in Python on top of the components already
present in `/workspace`: the stream generators, prequential evaluation
utilities, base classifier classes, and attribute observers.

Implement the stack in dependency order:

`VFDT`
A Hoeffding-tree learner for incremental decision-tree training and prediction.

`CVFDT`
A concept-drift-aware extension of VFDT with sliding-window management and
background replacement logic.

`ADWIN`
An adaptive windowing drift detector with the expected change-detection and
estimation behavior.

`MOA-style ensemble layer`
Add OzaBagging plus the interleaved test-then-train evaluation runner so the
online learners can be benchmarked the way the task expects.

`SAM-KNN`
Add the self-adjusting-memory kNN model with STM/LTM behavior for non-tree
stream learning.

Keep the public entry points the tests exercise, including:
`HoeffdingTree.train/predict/get_tree_size`,
`CVFDT.train/predict`,
`ADWIN.add_element/detected_change/get_estimation`,
`OzaBagging.train/predict`,
`EvaluateInterleavedTestThenTrain.run`,

experiment definitions. `run.sh` must execute the required experiments and
print one `EXPERIMENT_NAME: VALUE` line per reported metric.

id: "adwin"
title: "ADWIN: Adaptive Windowing for Concept Drift Detection"
category: stream_mining
requirement: |-
  ## Context
  You are building a data stream mining framework in Python. The base directory
  contains stream generators (RandomTreeGenerator, RotatingHyperplaneGenerator,
  WaveformGenerator), an evaluation framework (prequential evaluation), base
  classifier classes, and attribute observers. The VFDT (Hoeffding Tree) is
  already implemented in hoeffding_tree.py.

  ## Module: ADWIN (ADaptive WINdowing)
  Implement the ADWIN algorithm for detecting concept drift in data streams,
  based on: Bifet & Gavalda, "Learning from Time-Changing Data with Adaptive
  Windowing", SDM 2007.

  ### Algorithm Overview
  ADWIN maintains a variable-length window of recent items using an exponential
  histogram (list of buckets). When a change in distribution is detected via
  the Hoeffding bound, the older portion of the window is dropped.

  ### Implementation Requirements

  #### Bucket class
  - Stores summary statistics for a window segment: total sum, variance sum,
    and count of elements in this bucket.
  - Methods: merge(other) to combine two adjacent buckets.

  #### BucketRow class
  - Doubly-linked list of Bucket objects at the same granularity level.
  - Properties: size (number of buckets), head, tail.
  - Methods: add_to_tail(bucket), remove_from_head() -> Bucket.

  #### ADWIN class
  Main drift detector with exponential histogram compression.
  - Parameters:
    - delta: confidence parameter (default 0.002)
    - max_buckets_per_row: M parameter controlling compression (default 5)
    - min_window_length: minimum observations before checking (default 10)
  - Properties:
    - width: current total window length
    - total: running sum of all elements in window
    - variance: running variance estimate
  - Methods:
    - add_element(value: float) -> bool: Insert new observation, compress
      buckets if needed, then check for change. Returns True if drift detected.
    - detected_change() -> bool: Returns True if the last add_element detected
      a distribution shift using the Hoeffding bound.
    - get_estimation() -> float: Current mean estimate (total / width).
    - _compress(): Merge buckets when count at a row exceeds max_buckets_per_row.

=========== requirements/adwin.yaml
id: "adwin"
title: "ADWIN: Adaptive Windowing for Concept Drift Detection"
category: stream_mining
requirement: |-
  ## Context
  You are building a data stream mining framework in Python. The base directory
  contains stream generators (RandomTreeGenerator, RotatingHyperplaneGenerator,
  WaveformGenerator), an evaluation framework (prequential evaluation), base
  classifier classes, and attribute observers. The VFDT (Hoeffding Tree) is
  already implemented in hoeffding_tree.py.

  ## Module: ADWIN (ADaptive WINdowing)
  Implement the ADWIN algorithm for detecting concept drift in data streams,
  based on: Bifet & Gavalda, "Learning from Time-Changing Data with Adaptive
  Windowing", SDM 2007.

  ### Algorithm Overview
  ADWIN maintains a variable-length window of recent items using an exponential
  histogram (list of buckets). When a change in distribution is detected via
  the Hoeffding bound, the older portion of the window is dropped.

  ### Implementation Requirements

  #### Bucket class
  - Stores summary statistics for a window segment: total sum, variance sum,
    and count of elements in this bucket.
  - Methods: merge(other) to combine two adjacent buckets.

  #### BucketRow class
  - Doubly-linked list of Bucket objects at the same granularity level.
  - Properties: size (number of buckets), head, tail.
  - Methods: add_to_tail(bucket), remove_from_head() -> Bucket.

  #### ADWIN class
  Main drift detector with exponential histogram compression.
  - Parameters:
    - delta: confidence parameter (default 0.002)
    - max_buckets_per_row: M parameter controlling compression (default 5)
    - min_window_length: minimum observations before checking (default 10)
  - Properties:
    - width: current total window length
    - total: running sum of all elements in window
    - variance: running variance estimate
  - Methods:
    - add_element(value: float) -> bool: Insert new observation, compress
      buckets if needed, then check for change. Returns True if drift detected.
    - detected_change() -> bool: Returns True if the last add_element detected
      a distribution shift using the Hoeffding bound.
    - get_estimation() -> float: Current mean estimate (total / width).
    - _compress(): Merge buckets when count at a row exceeds max_buckets_per_row.
      Two oldest buckets at row i merge into one bucket at row i+1.
    - _check_for_change() -> bool: Scan from oldest to newest, checking if
      the difference between sub-window means exceeds the Hoeffding bound
      epsilon = sqrt((1/2m) * (4/delta') * ln(4n/delta')) where delta' is
      adjusted by window size and m = 1/(1/n0 + 1/n1).
    - reset(): Clear all state.

  #### ADWINExperiment class
  - Run drift detection on synthetic streams with various drift types:
    abrupt, gradual, and recurring drift.
  - Generate streams using numpy-style random with known change points.
  - Report detection delay and false positive rate.

  ## Experiments
  ### Experiment 1: ADWIN_DETECTION_DELAY
  - **What to measure**: Average delay (number of samples) from true drift point
    to detection on abrupt drift stream.
  - **Input/Setup**: Stream of 10000 samples, mean shifts from 0.0 to 1.0 at
    sample 5000. delta=0.002. Average over 5 runs with seeds 1-5.
  - **Expected output format**: ADWIN_DETECTION_DELAY: VALUE

  ### Experiment 2: ADWIN_FALSE_POSITIVE_RATE
  - **What to measure**: Fraction of false drift signals on a stationary stream.
  - **Input/Setup**: Stream of 10000 samples from N(0,1), no drift. delta=0.002.
  - **Expected output format**: ADWIN_FALSE_POSITIVE_RATE: VALUE

  ### Experiment 3: ADWIN_WINDOW_SIZE_STABLE
  - **What to measure**: Average window size on a stationary stream (should grow).
  - **Input/Setup**: Stream of 5000 samples from N(0,1). delta=0.002.
  - **Expected output format**: ADWIN_WINDOW_SIZE_STABLE: VALUE

  ### Experiment 4: ADWIN_WINDOW_SIZE_DRIFT
  - **What to measure**: Window size immediately after drift detection.
  - **Input/Setup**: Same as Experiment 1 setup, report window size at first detection.
  - **Expected output format**: ADWIN_WINDOW_SIZE_DRIFT: VALUE

  ### Experiment 5: ADWIN_MEAN_ESTIMATION_ERROR
  - **What to measure**: Absolute error of mean estimation vs true mean after drift.
  - **Input/Setup**: Stream shifts from mean=0 to mean=2 at sample 5000. Measure
    mean estimation error at sample 7000.
  - **Expected output format**: ADWIN_MEAN_ESTIMATION_ERROR: VALUE

  ## Instructions
  - Implement Bucket, BucketRow, and ADWIN classes in a new file `stream/adwin.py`
  - Implement ADWINExperiment in `stream/experiments/adwin_exp.py`
  - Update `run.sh` to run experiments and print results
  - Each result line format: `EXPERIMENT_NAME: VALUE`

  ## Files to modify
  - Create: stream/adwin.py
  - Create: stream/experiments/adwin_exp.py
  - Modify: run.sh

  ## Acceptance signals
  - `class Bucket` with merge method exists
  - `class BucketRow` with add_to_tail, remove_from_head exists
  - `class ADWIN` with add_element, detected_change, get_estimation, _compress
  - `class ADWINExperiment` exists
  - run.sh outputs all 5 ADWIN experiment values

title: "Mining Time-Changing Data Streams (CVFDT)"
category: stream_mining
requirement: |-
  ## Context
  You are extending the stream mining framework. VFDT (Hoeffding Tree) has been
  implemented and can learn from stationary streams. However, real streams often

  ## Context
  You have implemented VFDT (Hoeffding Tree) for stationary streams and CVFDT
  for concept-drifting streams. Now you will build the MOA evaluation framework
  which provides ensemble methods and standardized evaluation tasks.

  ## Module: MOA Framework
  Implement the MOA framework components:

  ### 1. OzaBagging Ensemble
  Online Bagging using Poisson(1) resampling (Oza & Russell, 2001):
  - Maintain an ensemble of N base Hoeffding Tree learners
  - For each training instance, each learner sees it K times where K ~ Poisson(1)
  - Prediction by majority vote across all learners

  Poisson(lambda=1) sampling:
  ```
  def poisson(lam):
      L = exp(-lam)
      k = 0; p = 1.0
      while True:
          k += 1; p *= random()
          if p <= L: break
      return k - 1
  ```

title: "SAM-KNN: Self-Adjusting Memory with kNN for Concept Drift"
category: stream_mining
requirement: |-
  ## Context
  You are building a data stream mining framework in Python. The base directory
  contains stream generators, an evaluation framework, base classifier classes,
  and attribute observers. VFDT, CVFDT, MOA, and ADWIN are already implemented.

  ## Module: SAM-KNN (Self-Adjusting Memory with k-Nearest Neighbors)
  Implement SAM-KNN, an adaptive classifier for data streams that maintains
  dual memory stores and uses kNN for prediction, based on: Losing, Hammer &
  Wersing, "KNN Classifier with Self Adjusting Memory for Heterogeneous
  Concept Drift", ICDM 2016.

  ### Algorithm Overview
  SAM-KNN maintains two memories: a Short-Term Memory (STM) that adapts quickly
  to the current concept, and a Long-Term Memory (LTM) that preserves stable
  knowledge. For each prediction, it evaluates which memory (or combination)
  provides better local accuracy, and uses that for the final decision.

  ### Implementation Requirements

  #### ShortTermMemory class
  - Sliding window of recent instances with FIFO eviction.
  - Parameters: max_size (default 5000)
  - Methods:
    - add(features, label): Add instance to STM, evict oldest if full.
    - knn_predict(query, k): Return majority vote of k nearest neighbors.
    - get_size() -> int: Current number of stored instances.
    - get_window() -> tuple: (features_array, labels_array)

  #### LongTermMemory class
  - Compressed knowledge store with cleaning and compression strategies.
  - Parameters: max_size (default 10000), min_cluster_size (default 10)
  - Methods:
    - add(features, label): Add instance to LTM.
    - clean(stm_features, stm_labels, k=5): Remove instances from LTM that
      are contradicted by the current concept in STM. An instance is
      contradicted if its kNN prediction from STM disagrees with its label.
    - compress(): Prototype-based compression using k-means clustering on
      stored instances per class. Replace cluster members with centroid.
    - knn_predict(query, k): Return majority vote of k nearest neighbors.
    - get_size() -> int: Current number of stored instances.

  #### SAMModel class
  Main classifier combining STM and LTM with adaptive memory selection.
  - Parameters:
    - k: number of neighbors (default 5)
    - stm_max_size: STM window size (default 5000)
    - ltm_max_size: LTM capacity (default 10000)
    - min_stm_size: minimum STM samples before using LTM (default 50)
    - ltm_clean_frequency: how often to clean LTM (default 500)
  - Methods:

      1. Add to STM.
      2. If STM evicts an instance, move it to LTM.
      3. Periodically clean and compress LTM.
    - predict(features) -> int: Predict class for query.
      1. Get STM prediction with local accuracy.
      2. Get LTM prediction with local accuracy.
      3. Return prediction from memory with higher local accuracy.
      4. If tied, prefer STM (recency bias).
    - _evaluate_memories(query, k) -> tuple: Compute local accuracy of
      STM-kNN and LTM-kNN on a validation window (last N instances of STM).
    - get_memory_sizes() -> dict: Return current STM and LTM sizes.

  #### Distance computation
  - Euclidean distance: sqrt(sum((a-b)^2))
  - Support optional feature weighting

  #### SAMKNNExperiment class
  - Run SAM-KNN on synthetic streams with abrupt and gradual concept drift.
  - Compare STM-only vs LTM-only vs combined SAM approach.
  - Track memory decisions over time (how often STM vs LTM is chosen).

  - **Input/Setup**: Same as Experiment 1.
  - **Expected output format**: SAM_STM_SIZE: VALUE

  ### Experiment 4: SAM_LTM_SIZE
  - **What to measure**: Final LTM size after processing stream.
  - **Input/Setup**: Same as Experiment 1.
  - **Expected output format**: SAM_LTM_SIZE: VALUE

  ### Experiment 5: SAM_MEMORY_DECISIONS

  - **Expected output format**: SAM_MEMORY_DECISIONS: VALUE

id: "vfdt"
title: "Mining High-Speed Data Streams (VFDT / Hoeffding Tree)"
category: stream_mining
requirement: |-
  ## Context
  You are building a data stream mining framework in Python. The base directory
  contains stream generators (RandomTreeGenerator, RotatingHyperplaneGenerator,
  WaveformGenerator), an evaluation framework (prequential evaluation), base
  classifier classes, and attribute observers for tracking split statistics.

  ## Module: Hoeffding Tree (VFDT)
  Implement the Very Fast Decision Tree (VFDT) learner, an incremental decision
  tree algorithm that grows from a data stream using constant memory per example.

  ### Algorithm
  The Hoeffding Tree uses the Hoeffding bound to determine when a leaf has seen
  enough examples to confidently choose a split attribute:

  1. Start with a single leaf (root).
  2. For each new example, sort it to a leaf and update sufficient statistics.
  3. Every `grace_period` examples at a leaf, attempt a split:
     a. For each attribute, compute information gain using the stored statistics.
     b. Let G_a be the best attribute's gain, G_b the second-best.
     c. Compute Hoeffding bound: epsilon = sqrt(R^2 * ln(1/delta) / (2n))
        where R = log2(num_classes), delta = split_confidence, n = examples at leaf.
     d. If G_a - G_b > epsilon, OR epsilon < tie_threshold (tau):
        Split the leaf on attribute a.
  4. Prediction: traverse to leaf, return majority class.

  ### Parameters
  - grace_period (n_min): 200 - instances between split attempts
  - split_confidence (delta): 1e-7 - Hoeffding bound confidence
  - tie_threshold (tau): 0.05 - threshold for forced tie-breaking splits
  - max_depth: 20

  - Class `HoeffdingTree` extending `AbstractClassifier` from classifiers.py
  - Use `NumericAttributeObserver` from attribute_observers.py for tracking stats
  - Support `train(instance)`, `predict(instance)`, `get_votes(instance)`

id: "adwin"
title: "ADWIN: Adaptive Windowing for Concept Drift Detection"
category: stream_mining
requirement: |-
  ## Context
  You are building a data stream mining framework in Python. The base directory
  contains stream generators (RandomTreeGenerator, RotatingHyperplaneGenerator,
  WaveformGenerator), an evaluation framework (prequential evaluation), base
  classifier classes, and attribute observers. The VFDT (Hoeffding Tree) is
  already implemented in hoeffding_tree.py.

  ## Module: ADWIN (ADaptive WINdowing)
  Implement the ADWIN algorithm for detecting concept drift in data streams,
  based on: Bifet & Gavalda, "Learning from Time-Changing Data with Adaptive
  Windowing", SDM 2007.

  ### Algorithm Overview
  ADWIN maintains a variable-length window of recent items using an exponential
  histogram (list of buckets). When a change in distribution is detected via
  the Hoeffding bound, the older portion of the window is dropped.

  ### Implementation Requirements

  #### Bucket class
  - Stores summary statistics for a window segment: total sum, variance sum,
    and count of elements in this bucket.
  - Methods: merge(other) to combine two adjacent buckets.

  #### BucketRow class
  - Doubly-linked list of Bucket objects at the same granularity level.
  - Properties: size (number of buckets), head, tail.
  - Methods: add_to_tail(bucket), remove_from_head() -> Bucket.

  #### ADWIN class
  Main drift detector with exponential histogram compression.
  - Parameters:
    - delta: confidence parameter (default 0.002)
    - max_buckets_per_row: M parameter controlling compression (default 5)
    - min_window_length: minimum observations before checking (default 10)
  - Properties:
    - width: current total window length
    - total: running sum of all elements in window
    - variance: running variance estimate
  - Methods:
    - add_element(value: float) -> bool: Insert new observation, compress
      buckets if needed, then check for change. Returns True if drift detected.
    - detected_change() -> bool: Returns True if the last add_element detected
      a distribution shift using the Hoeffding bound.
    - get_estimation() -> float: Current mean estimate (total / width).
    - _compress(): Merge buckets when count at a row exceeds max_buckets_per_row.
      Two oldest buckets at row i merge into one bucket at row i+1.
    - _check_for_change() -> bool: Scan from oldest to newest, checking if
      the difference between sub-window means exceeds the Hoeffding bound
      epsilon = sqrt((1/2m) * (4/delta') * ln(4n/delta')) where delta' is
      adjusted by window size and m = 1/(1/n0 + 1/n1).
    - reset(): Clear all state.

  #### ADWINExperiment class
  - Run drift detection on synthetic streams with various drift types:
    abrupt, gradual, and recurring drift.
  - Generate streams using numpy-style random with known change points.
  - Report detection delay and false positive rate.

  ## Experiments
  ### Experiment 1: ADWIN_DETECTION_DELAY
  - **What to measure**: Average delay (number of samples) from true drift point
    to detection on abrupt drift stream.
  - **Input/Setup**: Stream of 10000 samples, mean shifts from 0.0 to 1.0 at
    sample 5000. delta=0.002. Average over 5 runs with seeds 1-5.
  - **Expected output format**: ADWIN_DETECTION_DELAY: VALUE

  ### Experiment 2: ADWIN_FALSE_POSITIVE_RATE
  - **What to measure**: Fraction of false drift signals on a stationary stream.
  - **Input/Setup**: Stream of 10000 samples from N(0,1), no drift. delta=0.002.
  - **Expected output format**: ADWIN_FALSE_POSITIVE_RATE: VALUE

  ### Experiment 3: ADWIN_WINDOW_SIZE_STABLE
  - **What to measure**: Average window size on a stationary stream (should grow).
  - **Input/Setup**: Stream of 5000 samples from N(0,1). delta=0.002.
  - **Expected output format**: ADWIN_WINDOW_SIZE_STABLE: VALUE

  ### Experiment 4: ADWIN_WINDOW_SIZE_DRIFT
  - **What to measure**: Window size immediately after drift detection.
  - **Input/Setup**: Same as Experiment 1 setup, report window size at first detection.
  - **Expected output format**: ADWIN_WINDOW_SIZE_DRIFT: VALUE

  ### Experiment 5: ADWIN_MEAN_ESTIMATION_ERROR
  - **What to measure**: Absolute error of mean estimation vs true mean after drift.
  - **Input/Setup**: Stream shifts from mean=0 to mean=2 at sample 5000. Measure
    mean estimation error at sample 7000.
  - **Expected output format**: ADWIN_MEAN_ESTIMATION_ERROR: VALUE

  ## Instructions
  - Implement Bucket, BucketRow, and ADWIN classes in a new file `stream/adwin.py`
  - Implement ADWINExperiment in `stream/experiments/adwin_exp.py`
  - Update `run.sh` to run experiments and print results
  - Each result line format: `EXPERIMENT_NAME: VALUE`

  Wersing, "KNN Classifier with Self Adjusting Memory for Heterogeneous
  Concept Drift", ICDM 2016.

  ### Algorithm Overview
  SAM-KNN maintains two memories: a Short-Term Memory (STM) that adapts quickly
  to the current concept, and a Long-Term Memory (LTM) that preserves stable
  knowledge. For each prediction, it evaluates which memory (or combination)
  provides better local accuracy, and uses that for the final decision.

  ### Implementation Requirements

  #### ShortTermMemory class
  - Sliding window of recent instances with FIFO eviction.
  - Parameters: max_size (default 5000)
  - Methods:
    - add(features, label): Add instance to STM, evict oldest if full.
    - knn_predict(query, k): Return majority vote of k nearest neighbors.
    - get_size() -> int: Current number of stored instances.
    - get_window() -> tuple: (features_array, labels_array)

  #### LongTermMemory class
  - Compressed knowledge store with cleaning and compression strategies.
  - Parameters: max_size (default 10000), min_cluster_size (default 10)
  - Methods:
    - add(features, label): Add instance to LTM.
    - clean(stm_features, stm_labels, k=5): Remove instances from LTM that
      are contradicted by the current concept in STM. An instance is
      contradicted if its kNN prediction from STM disagrees with its label.
    - compress(): Prototype-based compression using k-means clustering on
      stored instances per class. Replace cluster members with centroid.
    - knn_predict(query, k): Return majority vote of k nearest neighbors.
    - get_size() -> int: Current number of stored instances.

  #### SAMModel class
  Main classifier combining STM and LTM with adaptive memory selection.
  - Parameters:
    - k: number of neighbors (default 5)
    - stm_max_size: STM window size (default 5000)
    - ltm_max_size: LTM capacity (default 10000)
    - min_stm_size: minimum STM samples before using LTM (default 50)
    - ltm_clean_frequency: how often to clean LTM (default 500)
  - Methods:
    - partial_fit(features, label): Update model with new instance.
      1. Add to STM.
      2. If STM evicts an instance, move it to LTM.
      3. Periodically clean and compress LTM.
    - predict(features) -> int: Predict class for query.
      1. Get STM prediction with local accuracy.
      2. Get LTM prediction with local accuracy.
      3. Return prediction from memory with higher local accuracy.
      4. If tied, prefer STM (recency bias).
    - _evaluate_memories(query, k) -> tuple: Compute local accuracy of
      STM-kNN and LTM-kNN on a validation window (last N instances of STM).
    - get_memory_sizes() -> dict: Return current STM and LTM sizes.

  #### Distance computation
  - Euclidean distance: sqrt(sum((a-b)^2))
  - Support optional feature weighting

  #### SAMKNNExperiment class
  - Run SAM-KNN on synthetic streams with abrupt and gradual concept drift.
  - Compare STM-only vs LTM-only vs combined SAM approach.
  - Track memory decisions over time (how often STM vs LTM is chosen).

  ## Experiments
  ### Experiment 1: SAM_ACCURACY_STABLE
  - **What to measure**: Prequential accuracy of SAM-KNN on stable stream.
  - **Input/Setup**: RandomTreeGenerator(seed=42, num_attributes=10,
    num_classes=2, max_depth=5), 10000 instances, k=5, stm_size=1000.
  - **Expected output format**: SAM_ACCURACY_STABLE: VALUE

  ### Experiment 2: SAM_ACCURACY_DRIFT
  - **What to measure**: Prequential accuracy after concept drift.
  - **Input/Setup**: Stream with abrupt drift at sample 5000 (mean shift).
    10000 total instances. Measure accuracy on last 2000 instances.
  - **Expected output format**: SAM_ACCURACY_DRIFT: VALUE

  ### Experiment 3: SAM_STM_SIZE
  - **What to measure**: Average STM size during evaluation.
  - **Input/Setup**: Same as Experiment 1.
  - **Expected output format**: SAM_STM_SIZE: VALUE

  ### Experiment 4: SAM_LTM_SIZE
  - **What to measure**: Final LTM size after processing stream.
  - **Input/Setup**: Same as Experiment 1.
  - **Expected output format**: SAM_LTM_SIZE: VALUE

  ### Experiment 5: SAM_MEMORY_DECISIONS
  - **What to measure**: Fraction of predictions where STM was preferred over LTM.
  - **Input/Setup**: Stream with drift at sample 5000. 10000 instances.
  - **Expected output format**: SAM_MEMORY_DECISIONS: VALUE

  ## Instructions
  - Implement ShortTermMemory, LongTermMemory, SAMModel in `stream/sam_knn.py`
  - Implement SAMKNNExperiment in `stream/experiments/sam_exp.py`
  - Update `run.sh` to run experiments and print results
  - Each result line format: `EXPERIMENT_NAME: VALUE`

  ## Files to modify
  - Create: stream/sam_knn.py
  - Create: stream/experiments/sam_exp.py
  - Modify: run.sh

  ## Acceptance signals
  - `class ShortTermMemory` with add, knn_predict exists
  - `class LongTermMemory` with add, clean, compress, knn_predict exists
  - `class SAMModel` with partial_fit, predict, _evaluate_memories exists
  - `class SAMKNNExperiment` exists
  - run.sh outputs all 5 SAM experiment values

requirement: |-
  ## Context
  You are building a data stream mining framework in Python. The base directory
  contains stream generators (RandomTreeGenerator, RotatingHyperplaneGenerator,
  WaveformGenerator), an evaluation framework (prequential evaluation), base
  classifier classes, and attribute observers for tracking split statistics.

  ## Module: Hoeffding Tree (VFDT)
  Implement the Very Fast Decision Tree (VFDT) learner, an incremental decision
  tree algorithm that grows from a data stream using constant memory per example.

  ### Algorithm
  The Hoeffding Tree uses the Hoeffding bound to determine when a leaf has seen
  enough examples to confidently choose a split attribute:

  1. Start with a single leaf (root).
  2. For each new example, sort it to a leaf and update sufficient statistics.
  3. Every `grace_period` examples at a leaf, attempt a split:
     a. For each attribute, compute information gain using the stored statistics.
     b. Let G_a be the best attribute's gain, G_b the second-best.
     c. Compute Hoeffding bound: epsilon = sqrt(R^2 * ln(1/delta) / (2n))
        where R = log2(num_classes), delta = split_confidence, n = examples at leaf.
     d. If G_a - G_b > epsilon, OR epsilon < tie_threshold (tau):
        Split the leaf on attribute a.
  4. Prediction: traverse to leaf, return majority class.

  ### Parameters
  - grace_period (n_min): 200 - instances between split attempts
  - split_confidence (delta): 1e-7 - Hoeffding bound confidence
  - tie_threshold (tau): 0.05 - threshold for forced tie-breaking splits
  - max_depth: 20

  ### Implementation Requirements
  - Class `HoeffdingTree` extending `AbstractClassifier` from classifiers.py
  - Use `NumericAttributeObserver` from attribute_observers.py for tracking stats

    27	def compute_hoeffding_bound(range_val: float, confidence: float, n: int) -> float:
    28	    """Compute the Hoeffding bound epsilon.
    29	
    30	    epsilon = sqrt(R^2 * ln(1/delta) / (2n))
    31	
    32	    Args:
    33	        range_val: Range of the random variable (R).
    34	        confidence: 1 - desired probability (delta).
    35	        n: Number of observations.
    36	
    37	    Returns:
    38	        The Hoeffding bound epsilon.
    39	    """
    40	    if n <= 0:
    41	        return float('inf')
    42	    return math.sqrt((range_val * range_val * math.log(1.0 / confidence)) / (2.0 * n))

    45	def compute_entropy(class_counts: List[float]) -> float:
    46	    """Compute entropy from class frequency counts."""
    47	    total = sum(class_counts)
    48	    if total <= 0:
    49	        return 0.0
    50	    entropy = 0.0
    51	    for count in class_counts:
    52	        if count > 0:
    53	            p = count / total
    54	            entropy -= p * math.log2(p)
    55	    return entropy

    58	def compute_info_gain(pre_split_counts: List[float],
    59	                      post_split_counts: List[List[float]]) -> float:
    60	    """Compute information gain of a split.
    61	
    62	    Args:
    63	        pre_split_counts: Class distribution before the split.
    64	        post_split_counts: List of class distributions for each branch.
    65	
    66	    Returns:
    67	        Information gain value.
    68	    """
    69	    pre_entropy = compute_entropy(pre_split_counts)
    70	    total = sum(pre_split_counts)
    71	    if total <= 0:
    72	        return 0.0
    73	    weighted_post_entropy = 0.0
    74	    for branch_counts in post_split_counts:
    75	        branch_total = sum(branch_counts)
    76	        if branch_total > 0:
    77	            weighted_post_entropy += (branch_total / total) * compute_entropy(branch_counts)
    78	    return pre_entropy - weighted_post_entropy

     7	class PrequentialEvaluator:

    11	    Accuracy is tracked over a sliding window or cumulatively.

    20	    def add_result(self, predicted: int, actual: int):
    21	        correct = 1 if predicted == actual else 0
    22	        self.correct_window.append(correct)
    23	        self.total_correct += correct
    24	        self.total_seen += 1
    25	        if len(self.correct_window) > self.window_size:
    26	            self.correct_window.pop(0)
    27	
    28	    def get_window_accuracy(self) -> float:
    29	        if not self.correct_window:
    30	            return 0.0
    31	        return sum(self.correct_window) / len(self.correct_window)
    32	
    33	    def get_cumulative_accuracy(self) -> float:
    34	        if self.total_seen == 0:
    35	            return 0.0
    36	        return self.total_correct / self.total_seen
    37	
    38	    def reset(self):
    39	        self.correct_window = []
    40	        self.total_correct = 0

    27	def compute_hoeffding_bound(range_val: float, confidence: float, n: int) -> float:
    28	    """Compute the Hoeffding bound epsilon.
    29	
    30	    epsilon = sqrt(R^2 * ln(1/delta) / (2n))
    31	
    32	    Args:
    33	        range_val: Range of the random variable (R).
    34	        confidence: 1 - desired probability (delta).
    35	        n: Number of observations.
    36	
    37	    Returns:
    38	        The Hoeffding bound epsilon.
    39	    """
    40	    if n <= 0:
    41	        return float('inf')
    42	    return math.sqrt((range_val * range_val * math.log(1.0 / confidence)) / (2.0 * n))

    45	def compute_entropy(class_counts: List[float]) -> float:
    46	    """Compute entropy from class frequency counts."""
    47	    total = sum(class_counts)
    48	    if total <= 0:
    49	        return 0.0
    50	    entropy = 0.0
    51	    for count in class_counts:
    52	        if count > 0:
    53	            p = count / total
    54	            entropy -= p * math.log2(p)
    55	    return entropy

    75	        branch_total = sum(branch_counts)
    76	        if branch_total > 0:
    77	            weighted_post_entropy += (branch_total / total) * compute_entropy(branch_counts)

    20	    def add_result(self, predicted: int, actual: int):
    21	        correct = 1 if predicted == actual else 0
    22	        self.correct_window.append(correct)
    23	        self.total_correct += correct
    24	        self.total_seen += 1
    25	        if len(self.correct_window) > self.window_size:
    26	            self.correct_window.pop(0)
    27	
    28	    def get_window_accuracy(self) -> float:
    29	        if not self.correct_window:
    30	            return 0.0
    31	        return sum(self.correct_window) / len(self.correct_window)
    32	
    33	    def get_cumulative_accuracy(self) -> float:
    34	        if self.total_seen == 0:
    35	            return 0.0
    36	        return self.total_correct / self.total_seen

"""Tests for the VFDT / Hoeffding Tree implementation."""

import os
import sys
import unittest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from classifiers import AbstractClassifier
from evaluation import evaluate_prequential
from hoeffding_tree import (VFDT, HoeffdingTree, HoeffdingTreeLeaf,
                            HoeffdingTreeSplit, VFDTExperiment)
from streams import Instance, RandomTreeGenerator


class TestHoeffdingTree(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_is_abstract_classifier(self):
        self.assertTrue(issubclass(HoeffdingTree, AbstractClassifier))
        self.assertIs(VFDT, HoeffdingTree)

    def test_public_api(self):
        tree = HoeffdingTree()
        for name in ("train", "predict", "get_votes", "get_tree_size"):
            self.assertTrue(callable(getattr(tree, name)), name)

    def test_single_leaf_before_training(self):
        tree = HoeffdingTree()
        size = tree.get_tree_size()
        self.assertEqual(size, {"num_leaves": 1, "num_splits": 0, "total_nodes": 1})
        self.assertIsInstance(tree.root, HoeffdingTreeLeaf)

    def test_predicts_majority_class(self):
        tree = HoeffdingTree(grace_period=10 ** 9)
        for _ in range(20):
            tree.train(Instance([0.1, 0.2], 1))
        tree.train(Instance([0.1, 0.2], 0))
        self.assertEqual(tree.predict(Instance([0.1, 0.2], 0)), 1)
        votes = tree.get_votes(Instance([0.1, 0.2], 0))
        self.assertAlmostEqual(votes[1], 20.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(votes[0], 1.0)

    def test_splits_on_informative_attribute(self):
        tree = HoeffdingTree(grace_period=50, split_confidence=1e-3, num_classes=2)
        rng = __import__("random").Random(7)
        for i in range(2000):
            x = rng.random()
            label = 0 if x < 0.5 else 1
            tree.train(Instance([x, rng.random()], label))
        self.assertIsInstance(tree.root, HoeffdingTreeSplit)
        self.assertEqual(tree.root.split_attribute, 0)
        self.assertGreater(tree.get_tree_size()["num_splits"], 0)
        # after the split the tree should be almost perfect
        correct = sum(1 for _ in range(500)
                      if tree.predict(Instance([(v := rng.random()), rng.random()],
                                               0 if v < 0.5 else 1)) == (0 if v < 0.5 else 1))
        self.assertGreater(correct / 500.0, 0.9)

    def test_max_depth_respected(self):
        tree = HoeffdingTree(grace_period=30, split_confidence=0.5,
                             tie_threshold=1.0, max_depth=2)
        rng = __import__("random").Random(3)
        for _ in range(5000):
            feats = [rng.random() for _ in range(5)]
            tree.train(Instance(feats, 0 if feats[0] * feats[1] < 0.25 else 1))
        self.assertLessEqual(tree.get_depth(), 2)

    def test_weighted_training(self):
        tree = HoeffdingTree(grace_period=10 ** 9)
        tree.train(Instance([0.5], 0), weight=5.0)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(tree.get_votes(Instance([0.5], 0))[0], 5.0)

    def test_hoeffding_bound_decreases(self):
        tree = HoeffdingTree(num_classes=2)
        self.assertGreater(tree.hoeffding_bound(10), tree.hoeffding_bound(1000))

    def test_accuracy_on_random_tree_stream(self):
        stream = RandomTreeGenerator(seed=42, num_attributes=10, num_classes=2, max_depth=5)
        tree = HoeffdingTree(num_classes=2, num_attributes=10)
        metrics = evaluate_prequential(tree, stream, 20000, window_size=1000)
        self.assertGreater(metrics["cumulative_accuracy"], 0.8)
        self.assertGreater(metrics["window_accuracy"], 0.9)
        size = tree.get_tree_size()
        self.assertEqual(size["total_nodes"], size["num_leaves"] + size["num_splits"])
        self.assertGreater(size["num_splits"], 0)

    def test_experiment_runner(self):
        exp = VFDTExperiment(num_instances=5000)
        results = exp.run_all()
        self.assertIn("VFDT_ACCURACY", results)
        self.assertIn("VFDT_TREE_NODES", results)
        self.assertGreaterEqual(results["VFDT_ACCURACY"], 0.0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

"""CVFDT: Concept-adapting Very Fast Decision Tree for time-changing streams.

Reference: Hulten, Spencer & Domingos, "Mining Time-Changing Data Streams",
KDD 2001.

CVFDT extends VFDT with four ingredients:

1. a sliding window ``W`` of the most recent ``w`` examples,
2. *forgetting*: when an example leaves the window its contribution is
   subtracted from every node statistic it once updated,
3. *alternate subtrees*: when a periodic ``CheckSplitValidity`` pass finds that
   the attribute used by an internal node is no longer the best one, a new
   subtree starts growing in the background at that node,
4. *replacement*: alternates are compared with the subtree they shadow on the
   incoming examples and take its place as soon as they are more accurate.
"""

import math
from collections import deque
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

from classifiers import AbstractClassifier
from hoeffding_tree import (HoeffdingTree, HoeffdingTreeLeaf, HoeffdingTreeNode,
                            HoeffdingTreeSplit)
from streams import Instance


class CVFDTLeaf(HoeffdingTreeLeaf):
    """Hoeffding tree leaf that can also *forget* an example."""

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        # Split attempts are driven by arrivals, not by the (window bounded)
        # weight currently stored in the leaf.
        self.instances_since_split_attempt = 0.0

    def learn_from_instance(self, instance: Instance, weight: float = 1.0):
        super().learn_from_instance(instance, weight)
        self.instances_since_split_attempt += weight

    def forget(self, instance: Instance, weight: float = 1.0):
        """Undo the effect of ``learn_from_instance`` for an expired example."""
        label = instance.label
        if label in self.class_counts:
            self.class_counts[label] = max(0.0, self.class_counts[label] - weight)
        self.weight_seen = max(0.0, self.weight_seen - weight)
        if self.weight_at_last_split > self.weight_seen:
            self.weight_at_last_split = self.weight_seen
        if not self.active:
            return
        features = instance.features
        for attr_index, observer in self.attribute_observers.items():
            if attr_index < len(features):
                observer.observe(features[attr_index], label, -weight)


class CVFDTSplit(HoeffdingTreeSplit):
    """Internal node that keeps split statistics and background alternates."""

    def __init__(self, split_attribute: int, split_value: float, depth: int = 0,
                 class_counts: Optional[Dict[int, float]] = None,
                 num_classes: int = 2, num_bins: int = 10,
                 nominal_attributes: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None):
        super().__init__(split_attribute, split_value, depth, class_counts)
        # alternate subtrees currently grown in the background at this node
        self.alternate_trees: List["CVFDTTree"] = []
        # error bookkeeping used to decide whether an alternate wins
        self.alt_error_counts: List[float] = []
        self.main_error_count = 0.0
        self.test_count = 0.0
        # sufficient statistics kept at the internal node for CheckSplitValidity
        self.stats_leaf = CVFDTLeaf(num_classes=num_classes, depth=depth,
                                    num_bins=num_bins,
                                    nominal_attributes=nominal_attributes,
                                    class_counts=class_counts)

    # -- statistics --------------------------------------------------------
    @property
    def attribute_observers(self):
        return self.stats_leaf.attribute_observers

    @property
    def weight_seen(self) -> float:
        return self.stats_leaf.weight_seen

    def learn_from_instance(self, instance: Instance, weight: float = 1.0):
        self.update_class_counts(instance.label, weight)
        self.stats_leaf.learn_from_instance(instance, weight)

    def forget(self, instance: Instance, weight: float = 1.0):
        label = instance.label
        if label in self.class_counts:
            self.class_counts[label] = max(0.0, self.class_counts[label] - weight)
        self.stats_leaf.forget(instance, weight)

    def get_best_split_suggestions(self, num_classes: int):
        return self.stats_leaf.get_best_split_suggestions(num_classes)

    # -- alternates --------------------------------------------------------
    def add_alternate(self, tree: "CVFDTTree"):
        self.alternate_trees.append(tree)
        self.alt_error_counts.append(0.0)
        self.reset_error_counters()

    def remove_alternate(self, index: int):
        del self.alternate_trees[index]
        del self.alt_error_counts[index]

    def reset_error_counters(self):
        self.main_error_count = 0.0
        self.test_count = 0.0
        self.alt_error_counts = [0.0] * len(self.alternate_trees)


class CVFDTTree(HoeffdingTree):
    """The growing engine used by :class:`CVFDT` (a VFDT with alternates)."""

    def __init__(self, grace_period: int = 300, split_confidence: float = 0.0001,
                 tie_threshold: float = 0.05, max_depth: int = 20,
                 num_classes: int = 2, num_attributes: Optional[int] = None,
                 num_bins: int = 10,
                 nominal_attributes: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None,
                 max_alternates: int = 1, alt_min_test: int = 500,
                 base_depth: int = 0):
        super().__init__(grace_period=grace_period, split_confidence=split_confidence,
                         tie_threshold=tie_threshold, max_depth=max_depth,
                         num_classes=num_classes, num_attributes=num_attributes,
                         num_bins=num_bins, nominal_attributes=nominal_attributes)
        self.max_alternates = max_alternates
        self.alt_min_test = alt_min_test
        self.base_depth = base_depth
        self.num_alternates_created = 0
        self.num_alternates_promoted = 0
        self.num_alternates_pruned = 0
        self.root: HoeffdingTreeNode = self._new_leaf(depth=base_depth)

    # -- node factories ----------------------------------------------------
    def _new_leaf(self, depth: int = 0,
                  class_counts: Optional[Dict[int, float]] = None) -> CVFDTLeaf:
        return CVFDTLeaf(num_classes=self.num_classes, depth=depth,
                         num_bins=self.num_bins,
                         nominal_attributes=self.nominal_attributes,
                         class_counts=class_counts)

    def _new_split(self, attr: int, value: float, depth: int,
                   class_counts: Optional[Dict[int, float]] = None) -> CVFDTSplit:
        return CVFDTSplit(attr, value, depth=depth, class_counts=class_counts,
                          num_classes=self.num_classes, num_bins=self.num_bins,
                          nominal_attributes=self.nominal_attributes)

    def _make_split_node(self, leaf: HoeffdingTreeLeaf, attr: int, value: float,
                         post_split_dists: List[List[float]]) -> CVFDTSplit:
        split_node = self._new_split(attr, value, leaf.depth, dict(leaf.class_counts))
        for branch_index in range(2):
            counts: Dict[int, float] = {}
            if branch_index < len(post_split_dists):
                for cls, cnt in enumerate(post_split_dists[branch_index]):
                    if cnt > 0:
                        counts[cls] = cnt
            split_node.set_child(branch_index,
                                 self._new_leaf(depth=leaf.depth + 1, class_counts=counts))
        return split_node

    # -- training ----------------------------------------------------------
    def train(self, instance: Instance, weight: float = 1.0,
              path: Optional[List[HoeffdingTreeNode]] = None):
        """Train on one example, also feeding every alternate on its path.

        ``path`` (when given) collects each node touched, so that :meth:`forget`
        can later subtract this example from exactly those statistics.
        """
        if weight <= 0:
            return
        if self.num_attributes is None:
            self.num_attributes = instance.num_attributes
        if instance.label >= self.num_classes:
            self.num_classes = instance.label + 1
        self.instances_seen += 1

        node = self.root
        parent: Optional[CVFDTSplit] = None
        branch = -1
        while not node.is_leaf():
            if node.alternate_trees:
                self._test_alternates(node, instance, weight)
            node.learn_from_instance(instance, weight)
            if path is not None:
                path.append(node)
            for alternate in node.alternate_trees:
                alternate.train(instance, weight, path)
            parent = node
            branch = node.branch_for_instance(instance)
            child = node.get_child(branch)
            if child is None:
                child = self._new_leaf(depth=node.depth + 1)
                node.set_child(branch, child)
            node = child

        leaf = node
        leaf.learn_from_instance(instance, weight)
        if path is not None:
            path.append(leaf)

        if leaf.active and leaf.instances_since_split_attempt >= self.grace_period:
            self._attempt_to_split(leaf, parent, branch)
            leaf.instances_since_split_attempt = 0.0
            leaf.weight_at_last_split = leaf.weight_seen

    def forget(self, instance: Instance, path: Sequence[HoeffdingTreeNode],
               weight: float = 1.0):
        """Subtract an expired example from every node it updated."""
        for node in path:
            node.forget(instance, weight)

    # -- alternate subtrees ------------------------------------------------
    def _test_alternates(self, node: CVFDTSplit, instance: Instance, weight: float):
        """Interleaved test of the main subtree against its alternates."""
        node.test_count += weight
        if predict_from(node, instance) != instance.label:
            node.main_error_count += weight
        for i, alternate in enumerate(node.alternate_trees):
            if alternate.predict(instance) != instance.label:
                node.alt_error_counts[i] += weight

    def _start_alternate(self, node: CVFDTSplit, attr: int, value: float,
                         post_split_dists: List[List[float]]):
        """Begin growing a background subtree that splits on ``attr``."""
        alternate = CVFDTTree(grace_period=self.grace_period,
                              split_confidence=self.split_confidence,
                              tie_threshold=self.tie_threshold,
                              max_depth=self.max_depth,
                              num_classes=self.num_classes,
                              num_attributes=self.num_attributes,
                              num_bins=self.num_bins,
                              nominal_attributes=self.nominal_attributes,
                              max_alternates=self.max_alternates,
                              alt_min_test=self.alt_min_test,
                              base_depth=node.depth)
        seed_split = alternate._new_split(attr, value, node.depth, dict(node.class_counts))
        for branch_index in range(2):
            counts: Dict[int, float] = {}
            if branch_index < len(post_split_dists):
                for cls, cnt in enumerate(post_split_dists[branch_index]):
                    if cnt > 0:
                        counts[cls] = cnt
            seed_split.set_child(branch_index,
                                 alternate._new_leaf(depth=node.depth + 1,
                                                     class_counts=counts))
        alternate.root = seed_split
        alternate.num_splits = 1
        node.add_alternate(alternate)
        self.num_alternates_created += 1

    def _evaluate_alternates(self, node: CVFDTSplit, parent: Optional[CVFDTSplit],
                             branch: int) -> bool:
        """Promote a winning alternate, drop a losing one.  True if promoted."""
        if not node.alternate_trees or node.test_count < self.alt_min_test:
            return False
        main_error = node.main_error_count / node.test_count
        best_index, best_error = -1, main_error
        for i, errors in enumerate(node.alt_error_counts):
            error = errors / node.test_count
            if error < best_error:
                best_index, best_error = i, error
        if best_index >= 0:
            self._promote_alternate(node, parent, branch, best_index)
            return True
        # no alternate is better than the current subtree: discard them
        for i in range(len(node.alternate_trees) - 1, -1, -1):
            if node.alt_error_counts[i] / node.test_count > main_error:
                node.remove_alternate(i)
                self.num_alternates_pruned += 1
        node.reset_error_counters()
        return False

    def _promote_alternate(self, node: CVFDTSplit, parent: Optional[CVFDTSplit],
                           branch: int, index: int):
        replacement = node.alternate_trees[index].root
        reindex_depth(replacement, node.depth)
        if parent is None:
            self.root = replacement
        else:
            parent.set_child(branch, replacement)
        self.num_alternates_promoted += 1
        self.num_splits = self.get_tree_size()["num_splits"]

    # -- CheckSplitValidity ------------------------------------------------
    def check_split_validity(self):
        """Re-verify every split, starting alternates where a better one exists."""
        self._check_node(self.root, None, -1)

    def _check_node(self, node: Optional[HoeffdingTreeNode],
                    parent: Optional[CVFDTSplit], branch: int):
        if node is None or node.is_leaf():
            return
        for child_branch, child in enumerate(list(node.children)):
            self._check_node(child, node, child_branch)
        for alternate in list(node.alternate_trees):
            alternate.check_split_validity()
        if self._evaluate_alternates(node, parent, branch):
            return  # this node has been replaced by one of its alternates
        self._check_split_attribute(node)

    def _check_split_attribute(self, node: CVFDTSplit):
        if len(node.alternate_trees) >= self.max_alternates:
            return
        if node.weight_seen < self.grace_period:
            return
        suggestions = node.get_best_split_suggestions(self.num_classes)
        if not suggestions:
            return
        best_gain, best_attr, best_value, best_post = suggestions[-1]
        if best_attr == node.split_attribute or best_gain <= 0.0:
            return
        current_gain = 0.0
        for gain, attr, _value, _post in suggestions:
            if attr == node.split_attribute:
                current_gain = gain
                break
        epsilon = self.hoeffding_bound(node.weight_seen)
        if (best_gain - current_gain) > epsilon or (epsilon < self.tie_threshold
                                                    and best_gain > current_gain):
            self._start_alternate(node, best_attr, best_value, best_post)

    # -- statistics --------------------------------------------------------
    def count_alternates(self) -> int:
        total = 0
        stack = [self.root]
        while stack:
            node = stack.pop()
            if node is None or node.is_leaf():
                continue
            alternates = getattr(node, "alternate_trees", ())
            total += len(alternates)
            for alternate in alternates:
                total += alternate.count_alternates()
            stack.extend(node.children)
        return total


def predict_from(node: HoeffdingTreeNode, instance: Instance) -> int:
    """Majority-class prediction of the subtree rooted at ``node``."""
    while not node.is_leaf():
        child = node.get_child(node.branch_for_instance(instance))
        if child is None:
            break
        node = child
    return node.majority_class()


def reindex_depth(node: Optional[HoeffdingTreeNode], depth: int):
    """Rewrite the depth of a grafted subtree."""
    if node is None:
        return
    node.depth = depth
    if not node.is_leaf():
        for child in node.children:
            reindex_depth(child, depth + 1)


class CVFDT(AbstractClassifier):
    """Concept-adapting VFDT with a sliding window over the stream.

    Args:
        grace_period: examples between split attempts at a leaf (n_min).
        split_confidence: Hoeffding bound confidence (delta).
        tie_threshold: forced-split threshold (tau).
        window_size: number of examples kept in the sliding window (w).
        check_frequency: examples between CheckSplitValidity passes (f).
        max_depth: maximum depth of the tree.
    """

    def __init__(self, grace_period: int = 300, split_confidence: float = 0.0001,
                 tie_threshold: float = 0.05, window_size: int = 10000,
                 check_frequency: int = 2000, max_depth: int = 20,
                 num_classes: int = 2, num_attributes: Optional[int] = None,
                 num_bins: int = 10,
                 nominal_attributes: Optional[Sequence[int]] = None,
                 max_alternates: int = 1, alt_min_test: int = 500):
        super().__init__()
        self.grace_period = grace_period
        self.split_confidence = split_confidence
        self.tie_threshold = tie_threshold
        self.window_size = window_size
        self.check_frequency = check_frequency
        self.max_depth = max_depth
        self.num_classes = max(2, num_classes)
        self.num_attributes = num_attributes
        self.tree = CVFDTTree(grace_period=grace_period,
                              split_confidence=split_confidence,
                              tie_threshold=tie_threshold, max_depth=max_depth,
                              num_classes=self.num_classes,
                              num_attributes=num_attributes, num_bins=num_bins,
                              nominal_attributes=nominal_attributes,
                              max_alternates=max_alternates,
                              alt_min_test=alt_min_test)
        # FIFO window of the w most recent examples plus the node path each one
        # updated, so expiring an example subtracts it from the right statistics
        self.window: deque = deque(maxlen=window_size)
        self._paths: deque = deque(maxlen=window_size)
        self.num_forgotten = 0

    # -- properties --------------------------------------------------------
    @property
    def root(self) -> HoeffdingTreeNode:
        return self.tree.root

    # -- learning ----------------------------------------------------------
    def train(self, instance: Instance, weight: float = 1.0):
        """Interleave window maintenance, tree growth and drift adaptation."""
        if len(self.window) == self.window_size:
            self._forget_oldest()

        path: List[HoeffdingTreeNode] = []
        self.tree.train(instance, weight, path)
        self.window.append(instance)
        self._paths.append(path)
        self.instances_seen += 1

        if self.check_frequency > 0 and self.instances_seen % self.check_frequency == 0:
            self.tree.check_split_validity()

    def partial_fit(self, instance: Instance, weight: float = 1.0):
        self.train(instance, weight)

    def _forget_oldest(self):
        """Drop the oldest example of the window and its statistics."""
        old_instance = self.window.popleft()
        old_path = self._paths.popleft()
        self.tree.forget(old_instance, old_path)
        self.num_forgotten += 1

    # -- prediction --------------------------------------------------------
    def predict(self, instance: Instance) -> int:
        return self.tree.predict(instance)

    def get_votes(self, instance: Instance) -> Dict[int, float]:
        return self.tree.get_votes(instance)

    # -- statistics --------------------------------------------------------
    def get_tree_size(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
        size = self.tree.get_tree_size()
        size["num_alternates"] = self.tree.count_alternates()
        return size

    def get_model_stats(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
        stats = self.get_tree_size()
        stats.update({
            "window_size": len(self.window),
            "alternates_created": self.tree.num_alternates_created,
            "alternates_promoted": self.tree.num_alternates_promoted,
            "alternates_pruned": self.tree.num_alternates_pruned,
            "instances_seen": self.instances_seen,
        })
        return stats

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        stats = self.get_model_stats()
        return (f"CVFDT(leaves={stats['num_leaves']}, splits={stats['num_splits']}, "
                f"window={stats['window_size']}, "
                f"alt_created={stats['alternates_created']}, "
                f"alt_promoted={stats['alternates_promoted']})")


class CVFDTExperiment:
    """Experiment runner comparing CVFDT and VFDT on a drifting stream."""

    def __init__(self, num_instances: int = 100000, window_size: int = 1000,
                 seed: int = 42):
        self.num_instances = num_instances
        self.window_size = window_size
        self.seed = seed
        self.results: Dict[str, float] = {}

    def _stream(self):
        from streams import RotatingHyperplaneGenerator
        return RotatingHyperplaneGenerator(seed=self.seed, num_attributes=10,
                                           num_drift_attributes=5,
                                           drift_magnitude=0.01,
                                           noise_percentage=0.05)

    def run_cvfdt(self) -> float:
        from evaluation import evaluate_prequential
        stream = self._stream()
        model = CVFDT(grace_period=300, split_confidence=0.0001, tie_threshold=0.05,
                      window_size=self.window_size, check_frequency=2000,
                      max_depth=20, num_classes=stream.num_classes,
                      num_attributes=stream.num_attributes)
        metrics = evaluate_prequential(model, stream, self.num_instances,
                                       window_size=1000)
        self.results["CVFDT_DRIFT_ACCURACY"] = metrics["cumulative_accuracy"]
        self.results["_cvfdt_window_accuracy"] = metrics["window_accuracy"]
        self.results["_cvfdt_stats"] = model.get_model_stats()
        return metrics["cumulative_accuracy"]

    def run_vfdt(self) -> float:
        from evaluation import evaluate_prequential
        stream = self._stream()
        model = HoeffdingTree(grace_period=200, split_confidence=1e-7,
                              tie_threshold=0.05, max_depth=20,
                              num_classes=stream.num_classes,
                              num_attributes=stream.num_attributes)
        metrics = evaluate_prequential(model, stream, self.num_instances,
                                       window_size=1000)
        self.results["VFDT_DRIFT_ACCURACY"] = metrics["cumulative_accuracy"]
        self.results["_vfdt_window_accuracy"] = metrics["window_accuracy"]
        return metrics["cumulative_accuracy"]

    def run_all(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        self.run_cvfdt()
        self.run_vfdt()
        return self.results

    def report(self):
        results = self.run_all()
        print(f"CVFDT_DRIFT_ACCURACY: {results['CVFDT_DRIFT_ACCURACY']:.4f}")
        print(f"VFDT_DRIFT_ACCURACY: {results['VFDT_DRIFT_ACCURACY']:.4f}")


def main():
    CVFDTExperiment().report()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
